segments.speaker: RECEPTIONIST
segments.en: Good evening, City Police Station. Can I help you?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh hello, I’d like to report a stolen briefcase, please.

segments.speaker: RECEPTIONIST
segments.en: Just a minute and I’ll put you through.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Lost property. Can I help you?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh, yes. I’ve had my briefcase stolen.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: OK … I’ll take some details … Tell me what it looks like, first of all.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well … it’s a soft leather one, you know, not a heavy box-type like a man’s.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Mmm … and how does it close?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It’s got buckles at the front ... two of them They’re gold-plated ones.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Fine … Was it locked?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: No, I’m afraid not.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Never mind. Any distinguishing features?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Pardon?

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Any marks or badges on it that make it stand out?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Only the brand name.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: And where’s that?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It’s on the back … at the bottom in the left-hand corner. It’s Sagi. Oh and there’s a scratch … it’s quite bad but small … directly above the brand name. I did it recently putting it on my bike.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Right, got that. So, what did you have inside the briefcase?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well all my papers from college. It’s so frustrating but, thank goodness for computers, I haven’t lost them completely!

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Yes, you’re lucky.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: I had my wallet in my pocket so I didn’t lose that but there were also my pens which I got for my birthday and a novel I was planning to read on the train.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Right. Where exactly did you lose the briefcase?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well … I couldn’t believe it. I was standing on the platform … it was right next to me.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: You were holding it?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: I’d just put it down on the floor but I could almost feel it beside me. I was watching for my tram because sometimes it comes early and then next time I looked, my briefcase wasn’t there.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: And what time was this?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Ah … it was … it must have been about 5.20 … no a bit later. I’d say 5.30 because it was just getting crowded and the train normally comes at about twenty-five to six.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Right, if you’ll just give me some personal details ...

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: What name is it?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: I’m Mary Prescott.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Can you spell that?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, it’s P-R E-S-C-O-T-T.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: And your address?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Flat 2, 41, Fountain Road, Canterbury.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Fountain Road.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, number 41.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: And have you got a contact telephone number?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, it’s 7-5 double 2-3-9.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: 7-5-double 239. Fine. One last question — what would you say the value of your briefcase is?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Including the contents?

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Yes, Just a rough estimate is fine.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: I’m not sure. Well, the briefcase itself is quite new; I bought it last month for £40. I suppose about £65. The contents are worth about 20 or 25 pounds at least.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: That’s fine. Well, if you could come down to the station tomorrow, you can sign this form and have a look at what we’ve got here.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK, thanks. 'Bye.

segments.speaker: POLICE OFFICER
segments.en: Goodbye.
